axes.model_access:
**Multi-model frontier routing — tiered per task rather than locked to a single model.**

Official "Why Amp" wording:

**"Multi-Model: GPT-5.6, Claude Fable 5, fast models—Amp uses them all, for what each model is best at."**

**The four Agent Modes are capability presets, not fixed model selectors**:
`low` / `medium` / `high` / `ultra`.

**Official wording**: "Modes are capability presets, not fixed model selectors"

Routing is customizable. It looks at connected provider subscriptions, workspace limits and model availability
to decide how the main agent and the Oracle run.

**The Oracle is a "second opinion" model.**

At `high`, the main agent uses GPT-6 Astra (medium) and the Oracle uses Claude Fable 5.1.
At low / medium / ultra, the Oracle defaults to GPT-6 Astra.

**BYOK is now open across all tiers** (official news notes: for all tiers since 2026-09-30).

Supported: OpenRouter, Bedrock, Google Cloud Agent Platform,
Azure Foundry, Vercel / Cloudflare AI Gateway, Ollama Cloud, OpenCode Go and custom endpoint URLs,
and ChatGPT subscriptions can be used too.

⚠ **The official sources disagree.** The security reference page still says:

**Official wording**: "Amp doesn't support Bring Your Own Key or self-hosted deployments"

This contradicts the BYOK stance on the pricing page / news; when citing, treat the pricing page as authoritative.
axes.runtime:
**Hybrid: local Client + cloud Server.** Threads can additionally run on three execution surfaces.

The official security reference splits Amp into two components.

**Amp Client** runs locally: code and context management, local settings, local thread history.

**Amp Server** is a multi-tenant cloud service on ampcode.com, hosted on GCP.
It handles authentication, thread sync and LLM proxying.

**Thread execution surfaces come in three**: local, **orb** (a machine Amp creates for you in the cloud),
**runner** (your own machine, `amp --no-tui --runner-id <id>`).

The CLI picks the execution location with `--executor local|orb|runner:<id>`.

There are also Web and macOS / iOS apps. The same agent, the same thread — usable everywhere.
axes.local_files:
**The Client carries only local context; the official explicitly does not index the whole repo.**

Official security reference wording:

"The Amp Client and Amp Server do not **see, store, clone, or index the entire codebase**"

It only sends the Server the code snippets / whole files selected as context
(partial code data).

Tool side: `Read` / `create_file` / `edit_file` / `glob` / `Grep` / `Bash` etc.

**IDE integration** (VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Zed, Neovim):
once connected, Amp can see the currently open file and selection.
It can also **edit files through your IDE, with full undo support**.
axes.background:
**There is a real background form — orbs.**

Official homepage wording:

"Run agents anywhere and they **keep working after you close your laptop**"

Each thread gets an orb (already carrying your code, tools and plugins); it keeps running after shutdown and can be continued from your phone.

**Runners live on your own machines**: `--share` can share a runner with the workspace,
so others can start threads on it from ampcode.com too (the machine must be on).

**Scheduling and self-wake**: the official manual has Schedules.

An official demo video shows the agent

**official wording**: "uses automations to wake itself up"

that is, waking up on schedule to check production.
axes.tools:
**Built-in tools + subagents + plugins + MCP — all four layers have official pages.**

**Built-in tools**: `amp tools list` shows `Bash`, `Read`, `create_file`, `edit_file`.
Also `glob`, `Grep`, `web_search`, `read_web_page`, `Task`, `todo_*`, `undo_edit`.

**Subagents / tools**: `oracle` (second opinion for complex reasoning),
**Librarian** (cross-repo retrieval. Can read all public GitHub code, and your private repos too),
**Painter** (GPT Image generation and editing), Search, Read Thread.

**Plugin system**: you can write custom policy plugins (including a permissions plugin example).
Custom agent modes and subagents are also possible.

**MCP**: local (`amp.mcpServers`, command / args / env, stdio) and
remote definitions (stored on ampcode.com, url / headers).

Transports include SSE and Streamable.

Auth includes automatic **OAuth**, bearer, **Amp ID token**, Workload Identity.

The official recommends packaging MCP servers into **skills** (`mcp.json`) — that keeps the tool list lean.
axes.context:
**Threads are the core unit — saveable, searchable, shareable.**

Official "Why Amp" wording:

**"Threads: You can save and share your interactions with Amp."**

You can @-reference other threads (URL or `@T-...`).
Past threads are searchable by keyword / file / repo / author / date.
Workspaces support **thread sharing and multiplayer**.

**AGENTS.md layering**: the official lists cwd / parent directories / subtrees, `$HOME/.config/amp/AGENTS.md`,
system-level `/etc/ampcode/AGENTS.md` and other layers.
A subtree AGENTS.md is pulled in when files in that subtree are read.

It also supports @-mention and globs conditional loading, and gives migration paths from CLAUDE.md / .cursorrules.

**Compaction**: the official Models page lists Compaction as "Context summarization for long threads".
axes.permissions:
**No approval by default — this is the point that most needs calling out.**

Official Tools page wording:

"By default, Amp **does not ask for approval** before running tools."

The official alternative is **custom policy plugins**
(distributable as workspace-level plugins).

**Workspace MCP servers require explicit approval.**
Servers in `.amp/settings.json` show `awaiting approval` on first detection; you need `amp mcp approve`.

Global settings and those passed via `--mcp-config` do not.

**The data side is fairly hard-nosed**: the official **auto-detects and redacts** common secrets.
(AWS / GCP / Azure, GitHub / GitLab, OpenAI / Anthropic, Stripe / Slack / npm etc.,
replaced with `[REDACTED:amp]`), but admits it is best-effort.

Thread data is stored on ampcode.com (GCP). **Your data is not used for training by default** (never enableable on Enterprise).
After deleting a thread, data is removed within 30 days; Enterprise offers zero data retention (ZDR).

**Subscriptions and BYOK quotas are two different things.** With your own key or subscription, there is no Amp token fee.
axes.fit:
Fits four usage patterns:

- people who want the agent to **run long on their own cloud machine (orb), continuing after the laptop closes**
- teams needing **multi-model frontier routing + an Oracle second opinion**
- people already working in the terminal or VS Code-family editors who want IDE hookup along the way
- organizations needing enterprise controls (SSO, audit logs, MCP allowlist, zero data retention)

sections.核验说明:
Why `confidence: partial`: most dimensions were verified against official pages.

Specifically: the runtime surface, execution surfaces, providers / modes, MCP hookup, permissions and the data side.

Two things were not verified. **First, the concrete quota difference between the Individual tier's Megawatt / Gigawatt levels**,
second, the body text of the official pricing page's "Questions & Answers".

The first is presented by the official as a toggle, never side by side on one page; the second was not expanded in this fetch. Hence no `verified`.

**Two official-source inconsistencies worth flagging**:

- ① the security reference page still says "no BYOK and no self-hosted deployments", contradicting the BYOK stance on the pricing page / news (treat the pricing page and recent news as authoritative)
- ② the task brief gave the npm package as `@sourcegraph/amp`, while the official install docs currently give **`@ampcode/cli` (officially marked not recommended)** — treat the official docs as authoritative

Official pages checked this round: homepage, pricing, Chronicle, Owner's Manual, docs/cli, docs/tools, docs/customize/mcp, Security Reference.

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs. The test protocol is at [protocols/coding/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/coding/_protocol.md).

**Suggested measurement**: focus on three things.

- ① the over-reach boundary of running tools under the no-approval default (whether only policy plugins backstop it)
- ② the orb's "keeps running after you close the laptop" behavior and pause-billing rules (the official cites 5 / 20 minute thresholds)
- ③ `amp --execute ... --stream-json` usability in scripts / CI (the official aims for Claude Code format compatibility)
unknowns:
- The **concrete quota difference** between the Individual tier's Megawatt and Gigawatt levels: the official pricing page presents them as a toggle, never side by side (orb-hour quotas on the official page; prices not stored per D9 policy)
- The **answer bodies** of the official pricing-page FAQ: this page captured only question titles; answer content was not expanded
- Orb concurrency limits and maximum single-run duration: the official does not state (checked docs/orbs and the pricing page)
- Self-hosted deployment: the official security reference says it is empty (explicitly unsupported); no self-hosted path is provided
